svg.font-family: Inter, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.text: Each main function is a group box holding its parallel sub-functions. The root fans to the seven functions;
pick the Layout System first (the star) — it shapes everything downstream.
Free-version sample — quality differs from the official release · the free version has limited layout functions
Arcgram system feature tree · group-box layout
A static image has no hover tooltip, so every node’s description is listed here.
An interactive node-and-edge diagram engine: one standalone HTML file, no build and no runtime. The AI draws the map of a system
(or of its own reasoning); the human audits and adjusts. This tree lays out Arcgram's own feature set — each main function is a
NODE GROUP BOX holding its sub-functions.
Pick the layout first — it's hard to undo. Three base shapes x an optional thinking overlay = six combinations, each suited to a
Parallel categories read top → bottom. Group nodes with COLUMNS. Best for lifecycles, build pipelines, and system maps.
Parallel categories read left → right. Group rows with BANDS (+ HCOLUMNS for the x-lanes). Best for roadmaps, layered
No categories — one causal / branching chain. Leave COLUMNS and BANDS empty; each node's role rides on its cat. Best for
Add diamonds to ANY shape and it becomes a thinking-flow: the engine colors the Y/N branches automatically. Best for decision
COLUMNS (v-lanes + tags), BANDS (h-phase stripes), the NODE GROUP BOX (group:true — this very diagram), HCOLUMNS, CANVASES
Get the diagram out as a shareable artifact, or render it inline. Fall back through the modes in order.
The Export button opens a modal that writes a self-contained HTML bundle — theme inlined, no external files needed.
Export a static SVG for a README, doc, slide, or print — where an interactive page can't run.
Checks the export is sound before it ships.
Render the engine inline via the host's HTML tool. Pan / zoom / hover native — best for iteration.
When Mode 1 is unavailable: write an inline SVG in the reply using arcgram conventions. Routes around the failed tool — don't
Write the engine + data to a file the user opens. Always available with filesystem access; the deliver-a-file mode.
Inspect a diagram as data — without rasterising the canvas. A stable contract for agents and scripts.
Returns { meta, logic, checkpoint, spec }: provenance, the logic graph, the Checkpoint verdict, and the declared @spec map.
The diagram as clean semantic nodes + edges, all geometry stripped. 'Results out, recipe in' — what the diagram means, not where
Geometry is opt-in only, via named profiles — so a consumer reading the default never breaks on a layout retune.
The sibling debug surface: geometry constants + internal layout stamps. Not a contract — may change between versions without
The typed boxes. Each node carries a render axis (type → color) and an optional reasoning axis (role) read by downstream agents.
session / sessionEnd / memory / doc / core / output / input / code / artifact / tool — plus a custom-type recipe. type is the
render axis: it resolves to fill + stroke color.
goal / action / decision / state / output. A semantic label for what the node does in the flow — read by downstream agents, not
A yes/no fork. Y branch → green check (down the spine); N branch → red cross (peels right). Author-sized; branch colors are a
status = a small theme-immune work-status dot (done / wip / open / frozen...). flag = a red bug marker on the top-right corner.
Each node's desc is a 1-3 sentence 'what is this and why does it matter'. Shown on hover; \n breaks lines.
One self-contained HTML file that renders and stays interactive in any browser — no server, no toolchain.
No build step, no npm install, no CDN, no runtime. The theme is inlined on export. Open the file in any browser.
Drag to pan, scroll to zoom, hover for a node tooltip. On-screen zoom controls and 'fit' shortcut; arrow keys pan.
Top-left tabs from CANVASES. Click a tab → its members stay bright while everything else dims to a spotlight. Click again to
A node can open a sub-diagram in-window — drill into a piece of the map without leaving the page.
A theme switcher. Semantic tokens (nodes, edges) adapt per theme; chrome tokens (controls) stay legible; status + crit colors
The diagram is a spec — check it, don't eyeball the render. Validators plus an on-canvas bug overlay.
Pre-draw structural check: catches dangling edges, orphan nodes, a diamond missing a branch, and duplicate ids.
Code ↔ diagram bijection: reconciles each node's declared @spec line against matching code. A no-code run reports INCOMPLETE,
The single entry: runs Checkpoint always, Reconcile when given code. The engine also self-checks on render and stamps the
The layout gate suite: collision, alignment, kink, density, hub readability, whitespace — each proven to catch its own violation
level: HIGH / MED / LOW. type: bug / logic-hole / geometry-defect. anchor: on a node, an edge, or a world-point.
A mark is open, then resolved as FIXED (check) or SUPERSEDED (warning, with a 'revives if' note). Draws a pulsing ring + reason
tag + a 'Known bugs' list; self-hides when clean.
How an agent authors a flow — the references to read and the hard rules that hold on every diagram.
SKILL.md (the workflow), schema.md (every field — the single source), layout-tips.md (positioning + routing heuristics). Author
node new-flow.mjs my-flow scaffolds a blank flow into output/. themes/ (base + default css) is the forkable palette.
Edit only the DATA section. Author from schema. The agent proposes; the human holds final write-authority. Keep the 'Made with
